questions.text: What does the source mnemonic CBABE represent?

answers.text: Cystic fibrosis, bronchitis, asthma, bronchiectasis, emphysema
Compliance, blood gas, airway, breathing, exercise

questions.text: The ATS definition in the source describes COPD as airflow limitation that is:

answers.text: Not fully reversible and usually progressive

questions.text: What is the primary test for diagnosing obstructive lung disease in the source?
Which airway resistance and compliance pattern is listed for obstructive disease?

answers.text: High airway resistance with normal or high compliance
Low airway resistance with low compliance only
Normal airway resistance with no compliance change
Absent airway resistance with fixed compliance

questions.text: Cystic fibrosis is caused by mutations affecting which protein?
Which pulmonary manifestation is listed for cystic fibrosis?

answers.text: Thick mucoid secretions that trap bacteria and cause recurring infections
Mean pulmonary artery pressure greater than 25 mmHg
Pleural space filled with blood after trauma
No airflow for at least 10 seconds during sleep

questions.text: Which sweat chloride result is positive for cystic fibrosis in the source?
How is chronic bronchitis defined in the source?

answers.text: Productive cough for at least 3 months per year for two consecutive years
Sudden pulmonary artery blockage by a clot
Permanent enlargement beyond the terminal bronchioles
Repeated episodes of no airflow during sleep

questions.text: Which cause is shared by chronic bronchitis and emphysema in the source?
The source's 'blue bloater' description is associated with:
Asthma airway obstruction is described as:

answers.text: Partially or completely reversible either spontaneously or with treatment

questions.text: In asthma pathogenesis, IgE on mast cells leads to release of which mediators?

answers.text: Histamine, leukotrienes, prostaglandins, and platelet-activating factor
Abnormal permanent dilation and thickening of airways from recurring infections
Fluid collecting in the pleural space from hydrostatic pressure
A genetic defect in sweat chloride testing only

questions.text: What is the standard diagnostic test for bronchiectasis in the source?
Which pattern fits emphysema in the source?

answers.text: Decreased FEV1/FVC and DLCO with increased lung volumes
Normal lung volumes and normal DLCO only
Positive sweat chloride test as the only diagnostic finding
